units.title: Holidays and Travel
units.intro: We talk about the **summer holiday** and **travel**. Grammar: the **past simple**, **pronouns**, **by / in / on**, comparatives, punctuation and **going to**.

cards.title: Talking about yourself
cards.task: Greet your partner. Tell them about yourself.

lines.text: Hello. Good afternoon.
Good afternoon. My name is Adem. I'm 13.
What do you like doing in your free time?
I like playing football. I don't like sweeping the floor.

body: Talk about: your name, age, where you live, brothers and sisters, what you like and don't like.

cards.title: What we did in the summer
cards.task: Write two sentences about what you did and two about your partner.
model: I [[worked]] in my mother's shop.
Sara [[went]] to Asmara with her family.
Kemal [[looked]] after his goats.
Asha [[watched]] a football match with her father.
body: The book's own examples (pp. 2–3).

cards.title: Summer in Segeneiti
paras: Senait lives in Segeneiti. In the summer holiday she picked **prickly pears** (beles).
The students used tins on sticks to take the fruit off the plants. They wrapped the fruit in leaves to break the needles.
They carried the fruit in buckets and baskets and sold it in the town.
The fruit was sweet and delicious. Camels and donkeys ate the skins.

questions.q: What did Senait do in the summer?
Why did they wrap the fruit in leaves?
questions.a: To break the needles and protect their hands.

questions.q: What two containers did they use?
Who ate the skins of the fruit?

cards.meaning: tasting very good
cards.example: They were very sweet and [[delicious]]!

cards.title: Past simple
rule: Regular verbs add **-ed**: help → helped, like → liked, fry → fried.
Irregular verbs change: come → came, eat → ate, drink → drank, cut → cut, make → made.

examples.text: In the summer holiday I [[helped]] my mother in her snack bar.
A lot of people [[came]] to the snack bar.
I [[fried]] eggs and [[made]] tea.
They [[eated]] food and [[drinked]] tea.

cards.pattern: verb + -ed, or the irregular past form

cards.title: He, him and his
rule: **He** is a subject pronoun. It goes before a verb.
**Him** is an object pronoun. **His** means belonging to him.

examples.text: Mussie went to Assab with [[his]] family.
[[He]] went to Assab with his family.
Mussie's family went to Assab with [[him]].
Mussie's family went to Assab with [[he]].
examples.fix: Mussie's family went to Assab with [[him]].

cards.q: Biniam's sister went to the market with ___ .
cards.why: After with we need an object pronoun (p. 9).

cards.title: Replacing names with pronouns
rule: Change the name to a pronoun. Keep the meaning the same.

examples.text: Fatna worked in the fields with her brother. → [[She]] worked in the fields with her brother.
Sara and Selam played football. → [[They]] played football.
Daniel's mother read with [[his]].

cards.title: The journey to Assab
paras: Every summer Mussie's family visits his uncle Habtom in Assab. Mussie likes fishing with him. His sister Almaz likes swimming.
Last year they **hired** a car. The journey was long and hot, and the baby cried. But they stopped to see ostriches.
This year they flew to Assab. It was their first time on a plane. It was more expensive, but it was **worth** it.
From the plane they saw the mountains, the sea and the islands. It was a beautiful **view**.

questions.q: Who is Habtom?
Why does Almaz like going to Assab?
questions.a: She likes swimming in the sea.

questions.q: How did the family travel this year?
Who stopped the car to see the ostriches?

cards.meaning: to pay to use something for some time
cards.example: They [[hired]] a car from a firm in Asmara.

cards.meaning: the way to go from one place to another
cards.example: Mussie's parents said that they should take a different [[route]].

cards.meaning: likely to bring enjoyment or benefit
cards.example: It was more expensive, but it was [[worth]] travelling by plane.

cards.meaning: what you can see
cards.example: It was a very beautiful [[view]].

cards.title: like / don't like + -ing
rule: Use **like + verb-ing** for things you enjoy. Past: **liked / didn't like**.

examples.text: Mussie [[likes visiting]] his uncle.
Mussie and Almaz [[don't like travelling]] by car.
I [[liked visiting]] my grandmother.
I [[didn't liked]] digging the garden.
examples.note: After didn't, use the base verb.

cards.title: by, in, on for transport
rule: **by** + transport, with no article: by bus, by car.
**in** + small transport you sit inside: in a car, in a taxi.
**on** + big transport or things you sit on top of: on a bus, on a camel.

examples.text: I travelled [[by]] bus to Keren.
I travelled [[in]] a car to Keren.
I travelled [[on]] a camel to Keren.
It was the first time the family travelled [[by a]] plane.
examples.fix: It was the first time the family travelled [[by]] plane.

cards.q: She went ___ her bicycle to the market.
cards.why: You travel on top of a bicycle (p. 14).

cards.title: Comparing adjectives
rule: Two things: **-er (than)**. More than two: **the -est**.

examples.text: The Keren bus is big.
The Tessenei bus is [[bigger than]] the Keren bus.
The city bus is [[the biggest]].
The city bus is [[the bigest]].

cards.title: Spelling rules
head: Rule
Examples
rows: most short adjectives: add er / est
ending with e: add r / st
one vowel + one consonant: double the last letter
big, bigger, biggest; hot, hotter, the hottest
ending with y: change y to i

cards.title: Song: I was going to Nakfa one day
body: I asked my friend **the fastest** way. She told me to go by car.
I asked my friend **the safest** way. By camel is the way to go.
I asked my friend **the nicest** way. "The bus is good," she said to me.

cards.title: Capital letters, full stops and question marks
rule: Use **capital letters** to start sentences and for names of people and places.
End a sentence with a **full stop (.)**; end a question with a **question mark (?)**.

examples.text: [[D]]o you know anyone in another country[[?]]
[[I]] have cousins in [[E]]ngland[[.]]
their names are michael and rahel
examples.note: Capitals for the start and for names.

cards.title: Rahel and Michael come to visit
cards.source: A letter from England / Rahel and Michael come to visit
paras: Roble's cousins, Michael and Rahel, live in London. They wrote a letter: they wanted to visit.
Roble went to Asmara airport by taxi with his brother. The plane was late, so they waited a long time.
The next day they travelled to Adi Keih by bus. Rahel enjoyed the view.
Then they walked ten kilometres to Roble's village, Safira. Michael and Rahel were very tired.

questions.q: How did Roble travel to the airport?
Why did they wait for a long time?
How did they travel to Safira?
Why did Michael and Rahel go to bed early?
questions.a: They were very tired from travelling.

units.title: Jobs and Money
units.intro: We talk about **jobs**, tools and **money**. Grammar: **want to be / would like to be**, **can**, **with / to / for**, **within / as**, a letter of request and the **present continuous**.

cards.title: want to be / would like to be
rule: Two ways to say the job you want: **I want to be ...** and **I would like (I'd like) to be ...**
He / she **wants** to be ...

examples.text: I [[want to be]] a teacher.
I [[would like to be]] a teacher.
Luchia [[wants to be]] a nurse.
Luchia [[want to be]] a nurse.

cards.title: The job I would like
cards.task: Write a paragraph: the job, why it is important, and two things you like about it.
model: I'd like to be a [[doctor]] because I think that [[health]] is very important.
I like studying science and caring for people.
I'm not afraid of blood. Working at night is not a problem for me.
phrases: I'd like to be a ... because ...
body: Almaz's paragraph from the book (p. 25).

lessons.title: What people do in their jobs

cards.title: Dictionary skills
body: A dictionary page shows the **headword**, its **pronunciation**, its **part of speech** and **examples of use**.

cards.title: A ... is a person who ...
rule: Use **a person who + present simple verb (-s)** to describe a job.

examples.text: A tailor is [[a person who makes]] clothes.
A mechanic [[repairs]] cars and lorries.
A pilot [[fly]] a plane.
examples.note: he / she / a pilot → verb + s.

cards.title: Lula
paras: Lula studied hard to **qualify** as a pharmacist. A pharmacist must go to college for **at least** five years.
At school she **achieved** very good results in science, especially chemistry.
When the five years were **over**, she returned home. Her family helped her buy a shop.
Lula knows the **theory** of health and disease. She gives advice and knows what medicine people should take.

questions.q: What is Lula's job?
Lula was good at chemistry in school. True or false?
Name two things Lula does for people.
questions.a: She gives advice, cleans and wraps cuts, and says which medicine to take.

cards.meaning: to learn enough to do a job
cards.example: Lula studied hard to [[qualify]] as a pharmacist.

cards.meaning: to get something by working hard
cards.example: At school she [[achieved]] very good exam results.

cards.meaning: an idea that explains something
cards.example: She studied the [[theory]] of health and disease for many years.

cards.title: can / can't for ability
rule: Use **can / can't + verb** (no -s, no to).

examples.text: I [[can speak]] English.
Hawa [[can't drive]] a car.
Jemal [[can use]] a computer.
Jemal [[can uses]] a computer.

cards.title: Jemal
paras: Jemal works in the **finance** department of a metalwork firm. He works with the company's money.
He calculates the money coming in and going out. He is very good at maths.
He writes the **accounts** on a computer.
At the end of every month the workers get their **salary**. They hand Jemal their slips, and he hands them cash.

questions.a: In the finance department of a metalwork firm.

questions.q: What does he use to write the accounts?
When is Jemal very busy?
questions.a: At the end of every month, when workers get their salary.

cards.title: with, to, for
rule: **with** + noun: hits nails **with a hammer**.
**to** + verb: used **to cut** wood.
**for** + verb-ing: used **for cleaning**.

examples.text: A carpenter hits nails [[with]] a hammer.
A saw is used [[to cut]] wood.
A mop is used [[for cleaning]].
A brush is used [[for sweep]] the floor.

cards.title: with, to, for: remember
body: **with** → a thing (noun): with a needle
**to** → a verb: to cut

A carpenter hits nails [[with]] a hammer.

cards.title: Two job advertisements
paras: HN Electronics needs a **secretary**. You must be able to use computers and speak and write English.
Hours: 8am to 12pm and 2pm to 6pm, Monday to Friday. Salary: 1500 Nakfa a month.
The Eritrean Lorry Firm is looking for lorry drivers. You need a clean driving licence.
Drivers can get up to 2000 Nakfa a month. Apply **within** ten days.

Monday **to** Friday = Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
work **as** a mechanic = in the job of.

lessons.title: Saturday job and the present continuous

cards.title: Applying for a job: the process
body: **First**, read the advertisement in the newspaper. **Next**, write a letter of application.
**Then**, complete an application form. **Finally**, go to an interview.

cards.title: Saturday job
paras: Amna is a student. Every Saturday she works in the cinema. She gets an income and sees many films.
People pay their **admission** at the desk. Then they give Amna their tickets.
It is dark, so she uses a small light to show people the way **ahead** to their seats.
After the film she cleans her **section**. She saves her money in a box and writes an account.

Why does she like her job?

cards.title: Present continuous and -ing spelling
rule: **am / is / are + verb-ing** for actions happening now.

examples.text: Ahmed [[is clapping]].
They [[are running]].
She [[is cutting]] the paper.
He is [[writting]] a letter.

cards.title: Money matters
paras: People get their **income** from work. Some work for the government or a company; farmers work for themselves.
If workers are not treated well, they may go on **strike**.
Doctors and lawyers must study for many years. These jobs are called **professions**.
When people are too old, they **retire**, so it is important to save. A bank pays you **interest** on your savings.
If you **owe** the bank money, you must pay interest to the bank.

questions.q: What is income?
questions.a: The money people get from work.

questions.q: Farmers work for themselves. True or false?

units.title: Health and Diseases
units.intro: We learn how to **stay healthy** and about common **diseases** in Eritrea. Grammar: **imperatives**, **conditionals with if**, adjectives, adverbs of **certainty** and **frequency**, semicolons and **plurals**.

cards.title: Staying healthy
paras: The best way to stay healthy is to eat healthy food, drink clean water and get enough sleep.
If you get sick, you could go to a **pharmacy**. The pharmacist knows a lot about health.
You could also go to a **clinic**, where you can see a doctor or a nurse. There are special clinics for pregnant women, babies and children.
If someone is very sick, they should go to a **hospital**.

questions.q: What are three ways to stay healthy?
questions.a: Eat healthy food, drink clean water, get enough sleep.

questions.q: Where should a very sick person go?
What is the best way to avoid malaria? (quiz)

cards.title: Imperatives
rule: An **imperative** gives instructions, orders, advice and warnings.
Use the base verb: *Be careful.* Negative: **Don't / Never + verb**.

examples.text: [[Wash]] your hands after you use the toilet.
[[Don't smoke]]! It's a very bad habit.
[[Never ride]] a bicycle at night without a light.
[[Washes]] your hands.

cards.meaning: something you often do
cards.example: Teach children good health [[habits]].

cards.meaning: simple
cards.example: Learn [[basic]] first-aid. It could save someone's life.

cards.title: Staying healthy on a journey
paras: A man took his family by bus to Tessenei. They took no water, so the children drank bad water and got sick.
In Tessenei the children played with small goats. They did not wash their hands before dinner, and got sick again.
Always wash your hands after touching any **creatures** (animals). When you travel, take a bottle of clean water.

questions.q: Why did the children get sick the first time?
questions.a: They drank bad water on the bus.

questions.q: Why did they get sick the second time?
questions.a: They didn't wash their hands after playing with goats.

questions.q: What does harm mean?

cards.task: Write five imperative sentences with good advice or warnings.

[[Never]] drink dirty water.
[[Try to]] boil water first.
[[Don't]] touch your mouth or eyes before your hands are washed.
[[Make sure]] you take a bottle of clean water on the bus.
body: Advice taken from the book's texts (pp. 47–48, 53).

cards.title: At the doctor's
cards.task: Read the conversation with a partner.

lines.text: How long has he been ill?
Two weeks. At the start he was very tired. This week he had diarrhoea and a bad headache.

No, just my head.

cards.meaning: a small amount of something

cards.title: Nurses give advice: STDs
paras: STD stands for **Sexually Transmitted Disease**. HIV is the most well known STD in Eritrea.
There are drugs for HIV, but no **cure**. Doctors may **combine** several drugs to help.
Herpes also has no cure. All other STDs can be cured with drugs, but some are serious.
Make good decisions: use condoms, or don't have sex until you get married. Clinics can test for all STDs.

questions.q: What does STD stand for?
Which two STDs have no cure?
What could happen if a woman gets chlamydia?
questions.a: She may not be able to have children.

cards.title: Conditional sentences with if
rule: The **if** clause is in the **present**. The other clause uses **will + verb**.
The if clause can come first (with a comma) or second.

examples.text: If we leave now, we [[will get]] to HalHal this afternoon.
If you take the drugs in this tube, you [[will feel]] better.
You [[will not have]] any money left if you buy that new jacket.
If you [[will take]] the drugs, you will feel better.
examples.fix: If you [[take]] the drugs, you will feel better.
examples.note: No will in the if clause.

cards.title: Adjectives
rule: An **adjective** describes a noun: young, tired, kind, red, new.

examples.text: The [[young]] boy was [[sick]].
The doctor is [[intelligent]] and [[kind]].
She came on a [[red]] bus.
She came on a bus [[red]].
examples.note: In English the adjective goes before the noun.

cards.title: Song: Healthy habits
body: **Always wash** your hands if you touch animals and when you use the toilet.
**Never drink** dirty water. **Try to boil** it first.
And **use** a mosquito net.

cards.title: Common diseases in Eritrea
paras: HAMSET teaches young people about the main diseases in Eritrea: HIV, AIDS, malaria, STDs and TB.
Many children and old people get sick from **malnutrition** (not eating properly) and diarrhoea.
People with TB must take special drugs every day for six months. This is hard for **nomadic** people.
Diabetes is increasing. It can affect **sight**: people with diabetes can go blind.

questions.q: Why is TB a big problem for nomadic groups?
questions.a: They move around, and the drugs must be taken every day for six months.

questions.q: Which sense can diabetes affect?
What does 'sight' mean?

cards.title: Remember HAMSET
body: HAMSET names the main illnesses that cause death in Eritrea.

cards.title: Present simple for regular actions
rule: Use the present simple for things that happen regularly. he / she / it: verb + **s**.

examples.text: She [[takes]] drugs for TB every day.
The doctor [[visits]] the village every week.
They always [[drive]] to the hospital in their car.
The doctor [[visit]] the village every week.
examples.fix: The doctor [[visits]] the village every week.

cards.title: Adverbs of certainty
rule: **maybe / perhaps** = something might happen. **probably** = a good chance.
**definitely** = it will happen; **definitely not** = it will not.

examples.text: Where is the cat? [[Maybe]] she's in the kitchen.
I will [[probably]] go to Asmara tomorrow.
What is 30 plus 20? It is [[definitely]] 50.
What is 30 plus 20? It is [[maybe]] 50.

cards.title: Role models with HIV and AIDS
paras: **Role models** are people who have done something good, so others want to be like them.
Gideon Byamugisha, a Ugandan priest with HIV, travels the world to talk about caring for people with HIV.
Musa Njoko from South Africa carried the Olympic Torch. People with HIV should be treated the same as everyone.
Magic Johnson, a basketball player, returned to play after finding out he had HIV.
The Sinikithemba choir ("We bring hope") sells CDs to pay for medical treatment.

questions.q: What is a role model?
questions.a: Someone who has done something good, so other people want to be like them.

questions.q: Why did Musa Njoko carry the Olympic Torch?
questions.a: To show people with HIV should be treated the same as everyone else.

cards.title: Semicolons and commas
rule: A **semicolon (;)** can replace a full stop to link two connected sentences.
A **comma (,)** shows a pause, for example between items in a list.

examples.text: Aiba is excellent at mathematics[[;]] last year she won the mathematics prize.
It is a beautiful day[[;]] the weather has been excellent all week.
She wants to become a doctor[[,]] a teacher[[,]] an engineer or a police officer.
Azeb is a polite intelligent girl.

lessons.title: Caring for a patient; how often?

cards.title: Caring for a patient with AIDS
body: Give the patient somewhere quiet to rest and put a mosquito net over the bed.
Boil drinking water and cook food properly. Keep drugs somewhere safe.
Give the patient some jobs in the house. Understand that the patient may get angry or sad.

cards.title: Adverbs of frequency
rule: **daily / weekly / monthly** go at the end of a sentence.
**occasionally** (sometimes) and **frequently** (often) go before the verb or at the end.

examples.text: I go to the clinic [[daily]].
Visitors [[occasionally]] come to my house.
Visitors come to my house [[frequently]].
I [[weekly]] play football.

cards.title: Malaria
paras: Most malaria cases are in Africa. Pregnant women and small children are most at risk.
People usually get malaria from **mosquitoes**. Only the anopheles mosquito carries malaria.
A mild case brings fever and vomiting. **Cerebral malaria** means malaria in the brain; it can lead to death.
The best way to prevent malaria is to use a mosquito net. If you think you have malaria, get a blood test.

questions.q: Who is most at risk from malaria?
What does cerebral malaria mean?
What is the best way to prevent malaria?

cards.title: Plurals
rule: Most words add **s**: apples, mothers.
Words ending in **sh, ch, s, x, z** add **es**: churches, buses, boxes.
Some words ending in **o** add **es**: potatoes, tomatoes, mosquitoes.

examples.text: I will put the food in [[boxes]].
There are many [[mosquitoes]] near my house.
I must buy [[matches]] and [[candles]].
I want to buy [[tomatos]].

lessons.title: The library and a health checklist

cards.title: Using the library
paras: You can learn about health **in general** and pregnancy **in particular** in the library.
In a library you must behave well, **particularly** keeping quiet.
Don't shout, steal, disturb other students or damage anything.
Return books to the correct place, and look after books you borrow.

questions.q: What things must you not do in the library?
questions.a: Shout, talk loudly, steal, disturb others or damage anything.

questions.q: What do dictionaries do?

cards.meaning: to give the meaning of a word
cards.example: I use a dictionary to [[define]] words, particularly long words!

cards.meaning: especially; more than others
cards.example: In general, I like watching TV, but I [[particularly]] like films.

2. [[Wash]] your hands after you go to the toilet.

4. [[If]] you think you have malaria, [[then]] get a blood test.

units.title: You and Other People
units.intro: We talk about **manners**, friendship and polite behaviour in different cultures. Grammar: present/past simple, **articles**, **adverbs of manner**, prepositions, letters and **telephone manners**.

cards.title: Manners
paras: Good **manners** means being polite to others.
A tired boy on a bus stood up and gave his seat to an old woman.
Something polite in one country may not be polite in another.
In China a **guest** leaves some rice to show he is full. Two French men finished their rice to be polite, so the Chinese **host** gave them more!

questions.q: Why did the boy give his seat to the old woman?
questions.a: The bus was full and she was standing; it is good manners.

questions.q: Why did the French men finish the rice?
Why did the Chinese man give them more rice?
questions.a: In China, finishing the rice shows you are not full.

cards.meaning: a person who invites people to their house
cards.example: They went out to a meal with a Chinese [[host]].

cards.meaning: a person invited to visit someone's house
cards.example: The [[guest]] does not finish the rice on the plate.

cards.title: Friendship or money?
body: **Value of money**: understanding how much everything costs.
**Value of friendship**: thinking that friends are more important than money.
In the story, Ali cheated his friend Salih when he sold Salih's goat.

cards.title: Ali's letter of apology
cards.task: Write a letter of apology to your friend Asha. You broke her bag and want to buy her a new one.
model: P.O. Box 4021, Asmara, Eritrea. 12-01-10
Dear Salih,
I am writing this letter to tell you that I'm sorry for cheating you.
We have been friends for a long time and my behaviour was really terrible. I got 400 Nakfa for your goat, not 259.
I will pay you the money I stole from you. I hope that you can forgive me and we can be friends again. I'm very sorry.
Your friend,
Ali Mohammed
phrases: I am writing this letter to tell you that I'm sorry for ...
I hope that you can forgive me.
body: Ali's letter from the book (p. 70): address and date, Dear ..., the apology, closing, signature.

lessons.title: Eden's week: present or past simple

cards.title: Eden
paras: Eden is a very good girl with a good **attitude** to life. She has a timetable.
She goes to school from Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 12:00.
Monday afternoon: shopping. Thursday afternoon: washing. Saturday morning: cleaning. Sunday morning: church.
On Tuesday and Sunday evenings she visits her friends. At other times she studies.

questions.q: What does Eden do on Monday afternoon?
When does she visit her friends?
What does she do on Saturday morning?

cards.title: Present simple or past simple?
rule: **Present simple** for things done regularly: every day, every Sunday.
**Past simple** for finished past time: yesterday, last Thursday.

examples.text: I [[do]] my homework every day.
Yesterday, Eden [[did]] the shopping.
Last Thursday Eden [[washed]] the clothes.
Eden [[study]] every day.

cards.title: It's not fair!
cards.task: Read the conversation. What do you think of Kemal and Neema?

lines.text: You haven't cleaned your room. It's a mess!
It's okay, I'll do it later.
No. First feed the dog, then clean your room and do your homework.
Why? It's not fair.
Because we're a family, and we have to help each other.

body: Shortened from the book's conversation (p. 73).

cards.title: a, an, the
rule: **a / an** = one thing in general. **an** before vowel sounds: an apple, an hour (but a university).
**the** = one thing in particular, or mentioned before. No a / an with uncountable nouns (water, oil).

examples.text: She lives in [[a]] house in Asmara. [[The]] house is small.
Do you want [[an]] apple?
I'll be back in [[an]] hour.
I study at [[an]] university.
examples.note: university starts with a 'y' sound → a.

cards.q: Neema said, "I've got ___ exam tomorrow."
cards.why: exam starts with a vowel sound (p. 73).

lessons.title: My family and me: adverbs of manner

cards.title: My family and me
paras: The writer is 17 and lives in a family of six. Her mother is a shopkeeper and her father is a pilot.
Her eldest brother **foolishly** didn't study hard and failed his exams.
She loves computers and wants a job where she can learn more about them.
Her mother wants her to work in the shop. She tells her mother **politely**, but her mother shouts **angrily**.

questions.q: Why was her brother foolish?
questions.a: He didn't study hard and failed his exams.

questions.q: Why is she arguing with her mother?
questions.a: Her mother wants her to work in the shop, but she wants to work with computers.

cards.title: Adverbs of manner
rule: Adverbs of manner say **how** people do things. Most come after the verb or the object.
Adjective + **ly**: careful → carefully. y → i: happy → happily. Irregular: good → **well**.

examples.text: She shouted [[angrily]].
She ate the meal [[quickly]].
We did our homework [[carefully]].
He plays football [[goodly]].

cards.title: It's wrong to lie
paras: Two sisters lied to their mother. They said they were visiting friends, but they went to the cinema.
After the film they got on a bus and went to a Chinese restaurant. They ate so much that the sister vomited.
Their mother found out. Their **punishment**: they could not go to their cousin's wedding.

questions.q: What did the sisters lie about?
questions.a: They said they were visiting friends, but they went to the cinema.

questions.q: What was their punishment?
questions.a: They could not go to their cousin's wedding.

cards.title: Prepositions
rule: **at** night, **at** school; **in** bed, **in** trouble; **on** foot, **on** the train.
get **on / off** the bus; **by** bus; **next to** the bank; cut **with** scissors.

Get [[off]] the bus here. The school is [[next to]] the bank.

paras: Many young children call their parents and friends by their first names. Older people are not always happy about this!
Some Eritrean children shout "You! You! You!" at **foreigners**. This is not polite in English.
Saying "hi" or "hello" is much more polite.
English speakers like to be more **formal**: Sir, Madam, Mr, Mrs, Miss or Ms.

cards.title: Cultural differences
paras: An Eritrean went to New York. Cars drove fast, and you must cross when the light is green.
In big shops much food is wrapped in plastic, so it was hard to **distinguish** the food he liked.
He invited an American woman to a restaurant. She paid for herself. He was angry.
At her house she did not **insist** that he eat and drink more. He felt insulted and left early.
Later he learned that in the USA it is not polite to insist. Polite behaviour differs between countries.

units.title: Music and Dance
units.intro: We explore **music and dance** in Eritrea and around the world. Grammar: likes and dislikes, **capitals**, a **letter of complaint**, **wh-questions**, persuasion, plurals with -y and **can / could**.

cards.title: Music and dance
paras: There are many types of music and dance. The radio plays traditional and modern cultural music, and American and British pop.
People listen to a **variety** of music: Afar and Nara music, hip-hop, ballroom, classical music for ballet, and pop.
Rahel from Barentu dances to traditional Kunama music at weddings. She also likes hip-hop.
Her parents prefer to listen to Eritrean **musicians**.

questions.q: What does 'musician' mean?
What does 'variety' mean?
What does Rahel say about Kunama music?
questions.a: She likes it and dances to it at weddings and celebrations.

cards.title: like / dislike
rule: **I / you / we / they like**; **he / she likes**. Add **really** for strong feelings.

examples.text: I [[really like]] Eritrean music and hip-hop.
She [[likes]] Tigre music.
We [[really dislike]] reggae.
She [[like]] Tigre music.

Yes, because our traditional music gives us a sense of national pride.
I don't agree. Foreign films are a good way to learn English.
Do you mean that we must combine the past and present?
Yes, young people must have a broad knowledge of culture.

rule: Use capitals for the important words in **titles** of films and books.
**Acronyms** (short names from first letters) are all capitals: EPLF, BBC.

Mr Abraham Goitom, Selam Music Shop, Asmara
Dear Mr Abraham,

At the second wedding the bride was full of **joy** because her grandmother was there. The family showed great **respect** to their guests.

paras: Eritrea has traditional instruments: the **krar** (played like a guitar), the **chira-wata** (like a violin) and the **kebero** (drums).
In some places men dance fast in a group called **assomeeya**; they jump and wave sticks.
In Kunama dances, people usually dance in couples.
Tigre and Bilen women dance the **sheleel**, shaking their long hair.
At the Eritrea Festival, Miriam most enjoyed the Saho dancing, because she had not seen it before except on TV.

units.title: Media and Communication
units.intro: We learn about **communication**, the **media**, advertising and **computers**. Grammar: plurals in -ves, **fact and opinion**, quotation marks and brackets, **more / the most** and giving **opinions**.

cards.title: Communication
paras: **Communication** means to make something known: to pass or exchange information or ideas.
Newspapers, radio and TV give many advantages. You can learn science, English and maths by watching TV.
If you don't get a newspaper, you may miss information about a new job. This is called **lack of information**.
Now communication is very fast. TV and the internet are two examples of **media**.

questions.q: What could people miss because of lack of communication?
How long does it take to gather world news now?
Give two examples of media.

cards.meaning: passing or exchanging information or ideas
cards.example: [[Communication]] is very important in a society.

cards.title: Media
paras: Media are what we use for sending or getting messages.
Newspapers, TV, radio, computers and the internet are **mass media**, because many people see and hear them.
A big school could use media as a **record** of its year: photographs, newspaper reports, interviews and exam **data**.
People who work in the media work for a newspaper, a TV company or a radio station.

questions.q: Give six examples of mass media.
questions.a: Newspapers, TV, radio, computers, the internet, and books, CDs or cassettes.

Some people say English films help people learn English. Others say young people may copy unsuitable clothes and violence.

units.title: Equal Lives
units.intro: We think about **equality** between women and men: sharing work, education and women's rights. Grammar: **as ... as**, the **past passive** and the **present perfect**.

cards.title: Song: We want Equality
body: We want **equality**, men and women treated **equally**
And we struggle hard wherever we may be
Because our women must be free.

cards.title: What is the song about?
body: Verse 1: a mother worked in the house all day with no thanks and no pay.
Verse 2: a sister was taken out of school for early marriage. All girls must finish education.
Verse 3: now we understand more. We're making progress day by day.

cards.title: Equal work
paras: Eden is a shopkeeper and Habtom is a carpenter. They both work hard.
Eden said, "I **object** to cooking the dinner every night. It's like having two jobs."
Habtom realised Eden **deserved** to rest as much as he did. He cooked pasta with tomatoes and onions.
Now they share the work: they take turns to cook, and they each wash half of the clothes.
Some people laugh, but most think Habtom is a good husband. He has a good **reputation**.

questions.a: In a shop (she is a shopkeeper).

cards.title: as ... as / not as ... as

**not as + adjective + as**: the first thing is less than the second.

**not as many ... as** = fewer.

There are [[not as many]] cars [[as]] buses on the road.

But not these: throw, low, slow, show, own, four, colour, cousin.

paras: At present fewer girls than boys go to school in Eritrea. The **majority** of secondary students are boys.
Some parents object to sending daughters to school, or want them to marry at 14 or 15.
The government is trying to **overcome** these problems. The law says no one should marry before 18.
Where there are female teachers, girls stay in school longer. Girls can **relate** to them.

questions.q: Who are the majority of students in secondary schools?
What does the law say about marriage?
questions.a: No person should get married before the age of 18.

questions.q: Why do girls stay in school longer where there are female teachers?
questions.a: They have people who can relate to them and encourage them.

cards.title: Women in the past
paras: Many years ago, in many countries, women were not allowed to vote.
Women put **pressure** on their governments. They chained themselves to government buildings and carried signs: 'Votes for women'.
Many women **were arrested** by the police. Some refused to eat and **were forced** to eat.
In time, women **were given** the same voting rights as men.

questions.q: What did the signs say?
What happened to women who refused to eat in police stations?

cards.title: Past passive
rule: The past passive shows that something happened **to** someone in the past.
Form: **was / were + past participle** (many are irregular).

examples.text: She [[was arrested]] (by the police).
The roads [[were blocked]] (by women demonstrating).
The chains [[were cut]] by the police.
The water [[was drinked]].

cards.q: The law ___ (change) so that women could vote.
cards.why: The law = one thing → was + past participle (p. 146).

cards.title: Dictionary skills
body: Many words have more than one meaning. Some words are nouns and verbs: *bend, chain, break*.
Find the first meaning for each part of speech.

cards.title: Women fighters
paras: In Eritrea's struggle for independence, 30% of the fighters were women.
The women showed that they could fight and work as well as men.
The National Union of Eritrean Women (**NUEW**) was started during the struggle.
Today NUEW teaches women reading, writing and maths, and works for equal rights.

questions.q: How many of the fighters were women?
What does NUEW do today?
questions.a: It educates women and works with the government for equal rights.

cards.title: Asha Jemal
cards.source: Asha Jemal: the first woman president of the biggest shoe factory
paras: Asha Jemal **was named** the first woman president of 'Smart Shoe' in Asmara.
She was born in 1960 in Keren and **was educated** there. She finished university in Asmara at 25.
In a bank, women were not treated equally. She asked questions, and she **was arrested** for five days.
Later she opened a food shop, and after independence she worked in government offices.

questions.q: Where was Asha born?
When did she complete university?
Why was she arrested?
questions.a: The police said she was creating problems in the bank.

cards.q: NUEW is an organisation of ...
cards.why: Women from all areas of Eritrea are part of the union (p. 147).

cards.title: Women's rights
paras: The government of Eritrea **has worked** hard to give women equal rights. NUEW **has helped**.
Women can represent the people in their towns and villages; 30% of the appointed people are women.
Women can do any job, own businesses and own land, and should get the same pay for the same work.
Some people **have not changed** their attitudes, so NUEW is educating people.

questions.q: Can women own businesses?
What is the law about marriage for girls?
Have women stopped fighting for their rights?

cards.title: Present perfect
rule: Use the present perfect when something in the past is **still true now**. Form: **have / has + past participle**.

examples.text: Adem [[has broken]] his leg.
I [[have done]] my homework.
Adem [[broke]] his leg last week.
Adem [[has broken]] his leg last week.

cards.why: things = plural → have + past participle (p. 151).

At the technical school she qualified as a mechanic. She is very good at her job.
Some men laugh when they see her with a spanner. I really admire Halima because she never gets angry.
Her work is [[as good as]] any other mechanic's.

units.title: Our Environment
units.intro: We learn about the **environment**: trees, energy, water, rubbish and a hotter world. Grammar: **first conditional**, **should/must/have to**, the **past continuous**, **apostrophes** and **going to/will**.

cards.title: Environment
paras: The **environment** is the conditions in which people, animals and plants live: land, air and water.
In many places people have damaged the land by cutting down trees.
In cities, factories and cars make a lot of smoke. This makes the air dirty.
Waste in rivers and the sea poisons fish, and the water is not safe to drink.
People need to stop harming the environment and start protecting it.

questions.q: What is the environment?
questions.a: The conditions in which people, animals and plants live (land, air and water).

questions.q: Why can factories and cars be bad for health?
questions.a: They make smoke, which makes the air dirty.

questions.q: How can we improve the environment?
questions.a: Stop harming it and start protecting it.

cards.title: Cause and effect with due to
rule: **due to** + the cause tells us **why** something happens.

examples.text: The land is damaged [[due to]] people cutting down trees.
The air is dirty [[due to]] factories and cars making smoke.
The water is not safe [[due to]] countries putting waste into rivers.
The air is dirty due factories.
examples.fix: The air is dirty [[due to]] factories.

cards.title: Good state or bad state?
head: Environment in a good state ...

the people cannot grow enough food.

the water is dirty and makes people ill.
there is enough fresh food for everyone.

lessons.title: Where have all the trees gone?

cards.title: Where have all the trees gone?
cards.source: Where have all the trees gone?
paras: Many years ago there were a lot of trees and a lot of rain in Eritrea. There were wild animals like elephants.
The number of people increased. People cut trees for firewood and for building houses.
Some traditional houses were built from more than one hundred trees each!
With fewer trees there was less rain, less grass and less food for animals.
Now the government has stopped people cutting trees. It is growing new trees with the people.

questions.q: Why did people cut the trees down?
questions.a: For firewood and to build their houses.

questions.q: What are new houses built from?
What do many people in towns use instead of wood?

head: Sentence from the text

body: **Fiction** books (literature) are stories. **Non-fiction** books give information.
Non-fiction is organised by subject: science, geography, history.
In every section, books are in alphabetical order by the writer's name.

cards.title: First conditional
rule: **If + present simple, will + verb** talks about a possible future result.
The if part can come first or second.

examples.text: If we have no trees, the soil [[will get]] washed away.
If we have good soil, we [[will grow]] a lot of crops.
If we have a lot of trees, the soil [[won't get]] washed away.
If we [[will have]] no trees, the soil will get washed away.
examples.fix: If we [[have]] no trees, the soil will get washed away.
examples.note: No will in the if part.

cards.q: If we drink dirty water, ...
cards.why: If + present simple, will + verb (p. 162).

cards.title: Words to describe the picture
body: The people are planting trees in **rows** on **terraces** on the hills.
Trees stop the **dust** and the soil from blowing and washing away.

cards.title: The problem with energy
paras: Many people burn wood for cooking, but Eritrea has lost 95% of its trees in the last hundred years.
Kerosene and gas save trees, but there is not much oil or gas left, and it is getting more expensive.
Burning wood, oil and gas makes smoke that poisons the air.
Near Assab the wind is strong. The government is building **wind turbines**, which make no smoke.
An Eritrean stove called **adhanet** uses much less wood, makes less smoke and is safer.

questions.q: How long will oil last, some scientists say?
What is the name of the new stove?
Wind energy is as expensive as energy from oil. True or false?

cards.meaning: if something doesn't happen
cards.example: We need different energy, [[otherwise]] many more people will become ill.

cards.meaning: activities to try to achieve something
cards.example: Many people are part of a [[campaign]] to stop burning oil and gas.

lessons.title: The world is getting hotter: should, must, have to

cards.title: The world is getting hotter
paras: **Carbon dioxide** (CO2) is a gas that holds the sun's warmth around the world.
Burning things makes a lot of CO2, so the world is getting too hot.
If the world gets too hot, there will be less rain and the ice at the Poles will melt.
Trees use CO2 to grow. We **must** plant more trees and we **have to** look after them.

questions.q: What is CO2?
questions.a: Carbon dioxide, a gas in the air.

questions.q: Why are trees important?
questions.a: They keep the soil firm and use carbon dioxide.

cards.title: should, must and have to
rule: **should**: something we think is right. **must**: stronger, often for rules.
**have to**: someone has told you to do it. Not needed: **haven't got to**.

examples.text: You [[should]] wash your hands before eating.
You [[must not]] cut trees down.
I can't play now. I [[have to]] take the cows to the river.
You must to wash your hands.
examples.note: No to after must or should.

cards.q: Which is a rule?

options.A: We must not poison our water.

cards.why: must is often used for rules (p. 167).

cards.title: Mai Abour
paras: The people of Mai Abour had enough water, but they were always ill with diarrhoea.
Cows defecated in the river, people used the mountain as a toilet and threw rubbish there.
Anwar **was sitting** by the river. His sister was ill. Genet saw a cow urinate in the water.
They told the elders. People boiled their water, built toilets and a drinking container for the cows.
Now the people of Mai Abour are healthy.

questions.q: What was making the water dirty?
questions.a: Animal and human waste and rubbish.

questions.q: Genet's sister was ill. True or false?
questions.a: False. Anwar's sister and Genet's grandfather were ill.

questions.q: What did Genet do with her rubbish?
questions.a: She burned it away from the water.

cards.title: Past continuous
rule: **was / were + verb-ing**: an action in progress at a time in the past.
Use the past simple for a short action that interrupts it.

examples.text: I [[was walking]] home when it [[started]] to rain.
Genet [[was watching]] Anwar's cows.
We [[were swimming]] in the river at three o'clock yesterday.
He carried water when I was meeting him.
examples.fix: He [[was carrying]] water when I [[met]] him.

cards.title: Apostrophes for possession
rule: **'s** shows something belongs to someone.
If the word already ends in s, add **'** at the end (s').

examples.text: This is [[Yasim's]] bag.
I went to my [[friends']] house.
Then he saw [[Genet's]] bucket.
This is Yasims bag.

cards.title: Apostrophes for contraction
rule: The apostrophe shows where letters are missing.
**it's** = it is / it has. **its** = belonging to it.

examples.text: [[I'm]] ill.
[[It's]] very sad that the river is dirty.
The dog was playing with [[its]] ball.
The dog was playing with it's ball.
examples.fix: The dog was playing with [[its]] ball.

cards.title: it's or its?
body: **it's** = it **is** / it **has**.
**its** = belongs to it (like his, her).

cards.title: going to and will
rule: **going to + verb**: already planned, or we can see it coming.
**will + verb**: a prediction, and in if-sentences. will not → **won't**.

examples.text: Look at the clouds. [[It's going to]] rain.
It [[will]] rain in June.
If the sea is poisoned, it [[won't]] be safe to swim.
If the sea is poisoned, it willn't be safe.
examples.fix: If the sea is poisoned, it [[won't]] be safe.

cards.title: Tesfay's plans
body: Planned: "I am **going to** demonstrate and campaign."
Prediction: "We **will** work to make the seas safe again."

cards.title: Rubbish
paras: A few years ago there were thin plastic bags everywhere in Eritrea. They blocked drains and harmed animals.
Plastic bags take 20 to 100 years to decompose. In 2005 the government stopped them.
Now people use cloth bags or baskets, which last for many years.
We should use things again: glass bottles go back to factories and food waste feeds goats.
Rubbish should be buried away from people, animals and rivers.

questions.q: What did the government do?
questions.a: It stopped factories making plastic bags and told shopkeepers not to give them (b and c).

questions.q: Glass bottles can be used again. True or false?
Food waste should be burned. True or false?

units.title: Crime
units.intro: We talk about **crime**, thieves, **bullying** and helping the police. Grammar: **must**, the **present perfect** vs **past simple**, **past continuous** and the prefixes **un-, dis-, il-, im-**.

cards.title: What is crime?
paras: Azieb: Crime is doing something against the **law**.
Zebib: A crime is an act against **society**, so it is an **antisocial** act.
Teacher: **Failure** to follow the law is also a crime.
A person is a criminal whether they are caught or not. But a **judge** must say so in a **trial**.
Crimes are different in different countries and times. Marriage at 14 is **legal** in some places and illegal in others.

questions.q: Is defining crime simple?
questions.a: No. It seems simple, but in reality it is not.

questions.q: Marriage at 14 is a crime in all countries. True or false?
Someone who commits a crime is called a ...
If someone is not caught, they are not a criminal. True or false?

cards.title: Crime words

Meaning

process in a court of law

cards.why: A trial is the process in a court of law (p. 181).

cards.title: Our goats are gone! (Part 1)
paras: It was eleven o'clock at night in Girmaika. Nejat **was reading** a book. She heard the dogs bark.
She thought it was a leopard. Her brother Nasser **was doing** his homework. He thought it was the wind.
Their parents **were sleeping**. Meriem and Osman were at their grandmother's house.
By eleven-thirty everyone was asleep.

questions.q: What was Nasser doing at eleven o'clock?
What did Nejat think was disturbing the goats?
What was grandmother doing?

cards.title: Past continuous questions
rule: Ask: **What was / were + person + doing?**
Answer: **He / She was ...ing. They were ...ing.**

examples.text: What [[was]] Nasser [[doing]] at eleven o'clock?
The dogs [[were barking]].
Meriem and Osman [[were listening]] to grandmother.
What were Nejat doing?

cards.title: Our goats are gone! (Part 2)
paras: In the morning the family found the goat **shed** broken and the goats gone. The dogs were dead from bad meat.
Nejat found two sets of footprints, one large and one small, so there were two thieves.
They found **clues**: a hammer, a piece of torn cloth and a saw. The barley was gone too.
Father: "We **must inform** the police." Mother: "Be careful. The thieves may be **violent**."

questions.q: What was NOT taken?
questions.a: The dogs (they were killed, not taken).

questions.q: How did they know there were two thieves?
Why did the dogs die?
questions.a: The thieves gave them bad meat.

cards.title: How will the story end?
cards.task: Write 5 or 6 sentences to finish Nejat's story.
model: I think the thieves first climbed the ladder over the wall.
Then they gave the dogs bad meat and broke the shed with a hammer.
The goats were taken out of the open compound door.
Nejat and her father are going to follow the footprints.
body: Use the clues on p. 186: ladder, meat, hammer, saw, open door.

cards.title: must / must not
rule: **must + verb** shows it is very important to do something.
Negative: **must not (mustn't)**.

examples.text: We [[must look]] everywhere.
I am cold. I [[must put]] on my jacket.
It is raining. We [[must not]] go outside.
We must to inform the police.

cards.title: Present perfect or past simple?
rule: **Present perfect** (has/have + participle): it happened, we don't know when.
**Past simple**: at a known time in the past.

examples.text: Someone [[has stolen]] our goats.
Someone [[stole]] our goats yesterday.
They [[have cut]] the fence here.
Last night, thieves have stolen our hens.
examples.note: Last night = known time → past simple.

cards.title: Prefixes un- and dis-
rule: A **prefix** goes before a word and changes it to the opposite.
Here **un** and **dis** mean **not**.

examples.text: [[untrue]] = not true
[[dishonest]] = not honest
[[unhappy]], [[unhealthy]], [[disagree]], [[disconnect]]

units.intro: We learn about **tourism** and follow Justin, a tourist from Norway, around Eritrea. Grammar: the **passive**, **many/much** and transport verbs.

cards.title: Tourism
paras: **Tourism** means visiting places in or out of your country. The main purpose is enjoyment.
A tourist stays outside their usual environment, for not more than a year, and does not work for money.
**International** tourism is travelling to other countries. **Domestic** tourism is travelling inside a country.
Tourists bring money for **development**: schools, roads, health facilities. They may also bring harmful things.
Tourists want good transport, accommodation, hospitality and health services. **Quality** matters, not only **quantity**.

questions.q: What is domestic tourism?
The only purpose of tourism is enjoyment. True or false?
questions.a: False. People also travel for other purposes.

Adey Lemlem: "**If** we work together, we can **solve** our problems and **raise** our **standard** of living."
Everyone clapped to support what the women **proposed**. A committee was formed.

cards.title: Simple or continuous?
rule: **Continuous** = be + verb-ing (am/is/are or was/were).
**Simple** = one verb form (play/plays or played).

examples.text: I [[was working]] at the hospital. (past continuous)
I [[am swimming]] in the sea. (present continuous)
The fighters [[ran]] towards their enemies. (simple past)
They are visit friends in Tio.

cards.title: Semira's story (Part 2)
paras: Semira's brother Dawit came home. Their house was destroyed. His mother and small brother had been killed.
Dawit went to the hospital in his fighter's uniform. On his gun was written **Victory to the Masses**.
They felt sorrow for their loss, but happiness for the victory. Semira was proud of Dawit.
Later she went to Sawa and joined the Naval Force. Now she is an officer who helps to **guard** the Red Sea coast.

cards.title: Joining with when, while, before, after
rule: **before / after**: one action happens before the other.
**while**: two actions at the same time. **when**: one short action during a longer one.

examples.text: I reached home [[before]] the rain started.
The rain started [[after]] I reached home.
I was washing [[while]] mother was cooking.
The radio was playing [[when]] I got up.
I reached home after the rain started. (I was home first)

cards.title: Comparing with adjectives
rule: Short adjectives: **-er than / the -est**. Long adjectives: **more ... than / the most**.

cards.source: Our visit to the Red Sea
paras: Students from Keren visited the Red Sea. It **connects** Africa to Asia and Europe.
They flew from Asmara to Assab, near the **border** with Djibouti. Soldiers of different **ranks** guard the **boundary**.
They travelled by car from Assab to Massawa. They visited the school at Tio and saw agriculture at Foro.
At Hirgigo they saw the electric power plant.

cards.title: Dictation tips
body: **Dictation** means writing down exactly what you hear.
Check capital letters, punctuation (full stops, commas, speech marks) and spelling.
When you dictate: read slowly, read each sentence 3 times, then read it all again.

cards.title: Contrast with but and though
rule: **but** and **though** join two contrasting (different) ideas.

examples.text: I think dictionary skills are easy, [[but]] vocabulary is difficult.
Many people live in Assab [[though]] it is very hot.
I don't know much about the Red Sea [[though]] I have visited Massawa.
Many people live in Assab because it is very hot.
examples.fix: Many people live in Assab [[though]] it is very hot.
examples.note: Heat is a reason not to live there → contrast.

cards.title: My year in Grade 7 English
cards.task: Write a paragraph with contrasting ideas about what you learned.
model: In Grade 7, I have enjoyed learning about Tourism because I like travelling.
I also enjoyed Music and Dance, but I did not like Crime because it was sad.
I did well in grammar though I need to improve my spelling.
phrases: I have enjoyed learning about ... because ...
I did well in ... though I need to improve ...
